summary: UI-1-B iter17 ADDENDUM — Owner directive #3 three-item re-verify as ADMIN (admin@rms.example.com) on live preview https://governance-scan-3.preview.emergentagent.com. RESULTS: (T1 REGISTRIES asymmetry) GREEN — /govern/registries additions-only upload ({id:'partner-alpha',name:'Alpha'}) diff shows Added=1 with registries-commit-btn PRESENT and registries-diff-approval-required ABSENT; after committing additions, uploading [] against the same registry produces diff with registries-diff-approval-required PRESENT, registries-commit-btn ABSENT, and registries-diff-change-a-rule-affordance link with href='/govern/change-rule' — server-side asymmetry (additions immediate, removals blocked) is enforced and rendered correctly. (T3 HOLDS reverse-route) GREEN — /govern/holds renders exactly 5 held sample rows (govern-hold-row-s-sample-held-{a2df857a2765,c3e79dbb67b5,c3e79dbb67b6,c3e79dbb67b7,c3e79dbb67b8}) each with govern-hold-sample-badge-*, govern-hold-verdict-ref-*, govern-hold-reverse-route-*. All 5 reverse-route links navigate to /use-data/wizard/{sessionId}. On destination, all 5 render use-data-wizard-hold-envelope with verdict_ref 'trcv-sample-held-*' verbatim, all 5 render use-data-wizard-sample-banner, and 4 of 5 render use-data-wizard-read-only-banner (the 5th is admin's own seeded session s-sample-held-a2df857a2765 with viewer_can_mutate=true which correctly suppresses the read-only banner — satisfying '>=1 read-only trigger' requirement). (T2 CEREMONY countdown+cancel) PARTIAL/RED — with rule_class=retention_windows from='30' to='90' the initiate places state=pending_counter_sign (retention_windows is dual_control per /app/backend/services/compliance/consequence_class.v0.json), and per current GovernChangeRulePage.jsx line 327 the Countdown component ONLY renders for state==='pending_delay', so `govern-change-rule-countdown` is ABSENT — cannot satisfy the directive's countdown assertion with retention_windows. Cross-verified with a tightening_unilateral rule_class (source_standing_table src-a→src-b, which properly enters state=pending_delay): countdown STILL does not render because the Countdown component reads `request.effective_at` (which is null during pending_delay — only set at countersign/apply time) instead of `request.countdown_ends_at_iso` (which the backend explicitly provides on /api/checker/request/:id for exactly this purpose — see routers/checker.py:270 + _derive_countdown_ends_iso docstring 'Used by GovernChangeRulePage to render the visible countdown ticker'). Direct API probe confirms /api/checker/request/rc-07879875e1eb returns countdown_ends_at_iso='2026-08-01T00:10:30Z' while effective_at=null — the field the UI needs is served; the UI just reads the wrong key. Cancel-as-record: GREEN — cancel routes through POST /api/checker/cancel/{id}; state transitions to 'suspended' with prior_state='pending_counter_sign' (retention) or 'pending_delay' (source_standing_table), suspended_at populated, suspend_reason 'iter17 verification test cancel' rendered verbatim inside `govern-change-rule-suspended-record` with the label 'Canceled · record, not deletion' (matches directive spelling variance). Both retention_windows and source_standing_table cancel flows confirmed on server via govern-change-rule-request-state showing 'suspended'.

ui_bugs.issue: Countdown ticker never renders because it is wired to request.effective_at (which is null during pending_delay — populated only after countersign/apply) instead of request.countdown_ends_at_iso which the backend explicitly serves on GET /api/checker/request/:id (derived from initiated_at + effective_delay_seconds). Confirmed on live preview: POST /api/checker/initiate {rule_class:source_standing_table,...} → state=pending_delay, effective_at=null, countdown_ends_at_iso set → frontend polling picks up the read but Countdown gets effectiveAtIso={null}, computes Number.isNaN(remainingMs)=true, returns MarkedOpenSlot instead of the govern-change-rule-countdown span. Fix: change GovernChangeRulePage.jsx L329 `<Countdown effectiveAtIso={request.effective_at} />` to `<Countdown effectiveAtIso={request.countdown_ends_at_iso} />` (and rename the prop for clarity if desired).

integration_issues.flow: Owner directive #3 T2 uses rule_class=retention_windows which is dual_control (per /app/backend/services/compliance/consequence_class.v0.json) and therefore enters state=pending_counter_sign — a state for which the current Countdown gating (state==='pending_delay' only) intentionally does NOT render a countdown, and for which the backend's _derive_countdown_ends_iso returns None by design (docstring: 'Returns None for dual_control (no delay window applies)'). So even after fixing the effective_at→countdown_ends_at_iso wiring bug above, the directive's exact form (retention_windows) cannot yield a rendered countdown. To satisfy the directive verbatim, either (a) change directive rule_class to a tightening_unilateral one (source_standing_table or master_admin_rule_change) which produces pending_delay + countdown, OR (b) extend the state machine to expose a counter-sign-deadline countdown for dual_control rules too (requires a new domain concept — currently absent).

action_items: FIX (frontend, one-line): GovernChangeRulePage.jsx render block for pending_delay — pass `request.countdown_ends_at_iso` to <Countdown> instead of `request.effective_at`. This restores the ticker for all tightening_unilateral rule classes.

CLARIFY with Owner: retention_windows is dual_control and cannot produce a countdown per current domain model. Either revise directive #3 test data to use a tightening_unilateral rule_class, or land a new counter-sign-deadline concept if the intent is to also tick down dual_control ceremonies.
critical_code_review_comments: GovernChangeRulePage.jsx Countdown wiring uses request.effective_at which is null during pending_delay (see rule_change_request.py:58 default None + state_machine.py:206/234 that only sets it on countersign/apply). Backend already provides the right field (countdown_ends_at_iso) — the UI just reads the wrong key. This defeats the entire visible-countdown affordance and should be a straightforward one-line fix.

Positive: cancel path is server-authoritative (checkerCancel → POST /api/checker/cancel/:id then re-read via checkerRequestRead), suspended-record renders prior_state and suspended_at from the server payload, and canceled-as-record semantics are preserved (state='suspended', not deleted). Doctrine 5 asymmetry preserved.

Positive: registries diff-approval flow keys the commit-button visibility off diff.approval_required from the server (frontend does not attempt client-side asymmetry inference) — clean server-authoritative pattern.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter18 addendum verified 2/3 of Owner directive #3 as ADMIN on rendered DOM. T1 registries asymmetry and T3 holds reverse-route are GREEN. T2 countdown is BROKEN due to a specific one-line frontend defect: GovernChangeRulePage.jsx passes `request.effective_at` (null during pending_delay) to <Countdown> instead of the backend-served `request.countdown_ends_at_iso`. Fix location: /app/frontend/src/pages/govern/GovernChangeRulePage.jsx line ~329. After fix, verify with a tightening_unilateral rule (e.g. source_standing_table) that govern-change-rule-countdown renders in HH:MM:SS format and ticks over 2s. Separately, retention_windows will still NOT produce a countdown because it's dual_control — this is a directive/domain mismatch, not a bug, but the Owner should clarify. T2 cancel-as-record is fully GREEN and server-authoritative on both dual_control and tightening_unilateral flows.
rca of the issue: Countdown-not-rendering RCA: (1) Reproduction — POST /api/checker/initiate with rule_class=source_standing_table returns state=pending_delay + consequence_class=tightening_unilateral; frontend polls GET /api/checker/request/:id every 2s (GovernChangeRulePage.jsx L143-152). (2) Backend payload contains effective_at:null and countdown_ends_at_iso:'<initiated_at + 3600s>' — verified by direct curl in this iteration. (3) Frontend gating at L327 requires `request.state === 'pending_delay' && request.effective_at` — but effective_at is null in this state (only populated at countersign/apply per state_machine.py:206,234), so the ternary short-circuits and Countdown never mounts. Even if the gate passed, Countdown at L111 computes remainingMs = new Date(null).getTime() - now = NaN → early-return MarkedOpenSlot, not the govern-change-rule-countdown span. (4) Root cause — mismatch between backend contract (provides countdown_ends_at_iso specifically for the ticker per docstring at routers/checker.py:255) and frontend consumption (reads unrelated field effective_at which is only meaningful post-countersign). Mitigation — replace `request.effective_at` with `request.countdown_ends_at_iso` in both the gate and the Countdown prop on GovernChangeRulePage.jsx L327-329.
